chapter: Fourteen years with Nat Cole and the recording sessions
title: Ashby recording Collins's 'Bop Kick' under his own name
summary: Ashby recorded Collins's melody Bop Kick with Nat and took credit; Collins did not hold it against him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: He recorded a tune with Nat, 'Bop Kick,' and that was my melody. The whole, I taught him the whole thing and he recorded this and put his name on there. The whole tune. You know, so consequently -- well, I never held it against him, it's all right, you know. Actually, this is a calculated risk when you do things like this. You know, when you teach people then you show them things like this, and it's not copyrighted, what are you going to do. You know, but I was a little surprised because I -- you know, I like to teach whether I get paid for it or not.
So I don't know, I think that they're friends of mine.

When I show them this and I do certain things for them I think that they're friends. I never think that they will take this and use it, and put their name on it. I was very disappointed with Ash, but after --- I liked him so much because Ash, despite that -- let me, you know, get this straight. Ashby is a tremendous -- he's a great guitarist. He's not just a good guitarist. Irvin Ashby is a great-- he's one of the giants. You know, and I admired him so much.

So you know, we sat down and I said well look Ash, look at this, let's go this way. Look, let's do this. And I was very surprised when I heard this record and it was note for note. And I'll tell you the name of the tune is Bop Kick. But as I said, previously, he wouldn't come around the group after I joined them and I wondered why. But later I found out -- I realized that this was why he didn't come. He was kind of embarrassed because of my being there and playing these things, and they realized that he had got these things from me, you know.
